topics.name: US Government Takes 10% Stake in Intel
topics.summary: The Trump administration converted $8.9 billion in CHIPS Act grants into a passive 9.9% equity stake in Intel, making the US government Intel's largest shareholder. The deal followed Trump publicly demanding Tan's resignation, a subsequent Oval Office meeting, and SoftBank's $2 billion investment. The stake is non-voting with no board representation, fueling debate over whether this constitutes socialism and concern over the slippery slope of government equity in private companies.

topics.name: Is the Intel Deal Socialism?
topics.summary: Debate over whether the government equity stake constitutes socialism. Socialists argue it doesn't qualify because it's passive, non-controlling ownership. Democrats criticized it as Marxist. The Trump camp framed it as art of the deal. Carl Behr's analysis argued ownership without control is not socialism and that liberals are opportunistically applying the label.

topics.name: SpaceX Starship Flight 10
topics.summary: SpaceX successfully completed Starship's 10th test flight, launching from South Texas, deploying dummy Starlink satellites, surviving dramatic re-entry with debris shedding, and splashing down in the Indian Ocean. Hosts discussed the pressure on SpaceX to meet Mars transfer window deadlines and the upcoming NASA Artemis moon landing requirement.

topics.name: Labubu and Pop Mart Phenomenon
topics.summary: Pop Mart's Labubu blind box toys have driven the company to a $55 billion valuation with 106% revenue growth. Hosts traced Pop Mart's history from a 2010 Beijing mall store through the 2016 Molly licensing deal, the 2019 Labubu licensing, and the 2020 Hong Kong IPO. TikTok unboxing culture and the inherent gambling mechanic of blind boxes were identified as key growth drivers. The most expensive Labubu ever sold for $170,000.

topics.name: Blind Boxes as Gambling for Children
topics.summary: Hosts argued blind boxes are effectively unregulated slot machines, drawing parallels to Beanie Babies, CSGO loot boxes, and sports betting. China has banned Labubu sales to children under 8. Hosts predicted American toy companies like Mattel and Ty will be forced to launch their own blind box lines.

topics.name: AI Hype Cycle and Expectations
topics.summary: Hosts debated where they are on the Gartner Hype Cycle for AI. John reported SF AI researchers told him deep learning is undefeated and pre-training scaling will continue, keeping his expectations inflated. Tyler and another host said they're heading toward the trough. Discussion included whether Dario Amodei extending timelines means the slope is just longer, not lower.

topics.name: Dr. Drew.com Dot-Com Era Story
topics.summary: Dr. Drew Pinsky appeared and corrected the hosts' earlier retelling of his SoftBank-backed dot-com company from 2000. He raised $10 million from SoftBank, built a team of 120 for a celebrity health and entertainment website, was advised to get big fast without a revenue model, and was in Goldman Sachs discussing a $30 million raise on a $110 million valuation the day the NASDAQ collapsed.

topics.name: Media Barbell Dynamics
topics.summary: Hosts and Dr. Drew discussed how value in media accrues to either the mega-platforms (YouTube, Spotify, TikTok) or individual talent (Joe Rogan, Andrew Huberman), with nothing viable in the middle. Traditional media corporations like late night shows are losing tens of millions annually while individual creators can build profitable businesses from home studios.

topics.name: Taylor Swift Engagement and Cultural Economics
topics.summary: Taylor Swift announced her engagement to Travis Kelce. Hosts discussed her 2014 WSJ op-ed predicting artists would control album pricing and how she partially got it right by creating scarcity through touring. They speculated the engagement could boost birth rates and consumer spending given her past impact on local economies during tours.

topics.name: Raw Milk Safety Debate
topics.summary: Dr. Drew weighed in after hosts mentioned Mark Cuban had called raw milk extremely dangerous. Drew listed real risks including brucellosis, tularemia, and listeriosis but argued the broader issue is society's irrational fear of low-probability risks driven by a loss of meaning and belief in mortality frameworks.

topics.name: AI Psychosis Claims
topics.summary: Dr. Drew expressed deep skepticism about AI psychosis reports, predicting they are vastly overblown and likely involve people who already had underlying psychiatric conditions. He also warned about the psychiatric risks of psychedelics common in AI culture.

topics.name: CHIPS Act and Semiconductor Policy
topics.summary: Detailed discussion of the CHIPS Act's slow rollout, Intel's $11 billion in grants and $11 billion in loans, and the strategic question of whether the US can realistically compete in trailing-edge manufacturing or should focus on leading-edge through TSMC and Samsung fabs being built domestically.

key_claims: The US government will own 9.9% of Intel as a passive, non-voting shareholder with no board representation after converting $8.9 billion in CHIPS Act grants into equity.
Intel lost $18.8 billion on $50 billion in revenue last year, but hosts argued it is not on the verge of bankruptcy and could survive without the grants.
The most expensive Labubu ever sold for $170,000 in June 2025; the most expensive Beanie Baby ever sold for approximately $500,000.
Pop Mart revenue grew 106% year-over-year to $1.8 billion, with $700 million from international sales; the company beat its full-year 2024 revenue in just the first half of 2025.
Pop Mart founder Wang Ning is now China's 10th richest person worth $28 billion.
Build-A-Bear stock is up 4,703% over the past five years.
SpaceX Starship is 403 feet tall, taller than the Statue of Liberty at 305 feet.
United Airlines now offers Starlink internet at 300 megabits per second, roughly 6,000 times faster than 56K dial-up.
Trump administration also struck a deal with Nvidia and AMD for the federal government to take 15% of their chip sales to China in return for allowing the exports.
SoftBank had previously discussed a potential deal to acquire Intel's chip manufacturing business entirely.
China banned the sale of Labubu blind boxes to children under 8 years old.
Leopold Aschenbrenner's fund was reportedly long Intel; hosts argued this aligned with his AI nationalization thesis rather than constituting insider trading.
Dr. Drew raised $10 million from SoftBank for Dr. Drew.com in 2000 and was in Goldman Sachs discussing a $30 million raise on a $110 million valuation the day the NASDAQ collapsed.
Cadence Design Systems agreed to pay $140 million for violating US export restrictions by selling banned technology to a Chinese National Defense University while Tan was CEO.

The Trump administration proposed a provision allowing the government to acquire an additional 5% of Intel at a discount if Intel sells a majority of its manufacturing business, acting as a poison pill against exiting manufacturing.
Bill Gurley argued that if the government is truly the lender of last resort, it should take 100% equity, citing failures to do so with GM, Goldman Sachs, and airlines.
Dr. Drew said he drank a liter of raw milk every day for two years with no ill effects, while acknowledging real risks of brucellosis, tularemia, and listeriosis.
SpaceX is pushing for an uncrewed Starship mission to Mars in 2026 to hit the orbital transfer window, with Musk acknowledging the goal will be tough.
